name: Thanh Toan Bridge
kicker: Tiled bridge in the vegetable plots
summary: An 18th-century tiled-roof bridge in the vegetable plots of Thủy Thanh, about 8 km southeast of Hue, with a shrine to its patron, Trần Thị Đào, in the middle bay. Cycle out past the plots and the small footbridges, then walk under the roof. Go for the village countryside on a bicycle morning.
getThere: About 8 km southeast to Thủy Thanh, by bicycle.
heroCaption: The tiled roof of Thanh Toan Bridge over the lilies

notice.title: No published fee or hours
notice.body: No ticket price or closing time is published for the bridge. Ask in the village.

body: Thanh Toan is about 8 kilometres southeast of the centre, in Thủy Thanh commune, Hương Thủy. Vietnam Tourism sends you there by bicycle, past vegetable plots and small footbridges.

The bridge is about 17 metres long and about 4 metres wide, divided into seven bays under the tiled roof (a later national article gives a slightly different length). The middle bay is a shrine to Trần Thị Đào, who paid for the bridge in the 18th century so the village could cross.

figures.caption: The decorated portal of the tiled bridge
figures.alt: A carved portal under the tiled roof of Thanh Toan Bridge

gettingThere: From the south bank, cycle southeast about 8 km to Thủy Thanh, Hương Thủy, through the vegetable plots.
admissionNote: Check on arrival. The national tourism page prints no fee.
